small_guidance:
- The conv-transpose GEMM kernel currently uses `tl.dot(w_tile, tl.trans(x_tile))` — load `x_tile` as `[BLOCK_K, BLOCK_SP]` directly (swap the index order so K is the row) so the dot is `tl.dot(w_tile, x_tile)` without an explicit transpose; this saves a shared-memory shuffle and unlocks larger tiles.
- Add autotune configs with `BLOCK_OC=128, BLOCK_SP=256, BLOCK_K=32` and `BLOCK_OC=256, BLOCK_SP=64, BLOCK_K=32` (num_warps=8, num_stages=3) — with H_OUT=W_OUT=34 (1156 spatial) and OC=128, larger SP tiles cut the per-program K-loop overhead and amortize the weight loads.
- Pre-pack `w_packed` as a registered buffer in `__init__` (not lazily on first forward) and store it in `[OC, IC*KH*KW]` already-contiguous; also consider pre-permuting to `[K_TOTAL, OC]` so the weight load in the K-loop is contiguous along K and the dot becomes `tl.dot(tl.trans(w_tile), x_tile)` only once outside the loop is unnecessary — pick whichever layout makes both loads coalesce on the K axis.
large_guidance:
- With `stride=1, padding=1, kernel=5`, ConvTranspose2d is equivalent to a *regular* Conv2d with padding=`KH-1-padding`=3 and a spatially-flipped weight — rewrite as a standard im2col conv (gather, not scatter), which has a much simpler index pattern (no `ih = oh+pad-kh` sign games) and lets you use a straight GEMM with `BLOCK_M=OC, BLOCK_N=spatial, BLOCK_K=IC*KH*KW`. This is the single biggest structural win available.
- Switch the conv kernel to channels-last (NHWC) input/output layout: the K dimension of the GEMM is `IC*KH*KW`, and contiguous IC makes the inner K stride unit-stride for both x and w loads. Materialize NHWC once at the start of forward and keep it through to the fused BN+tanh+pool+GN epilogue (which then also reads channel-contiguous data).
- Fuse the conv epilogue (BN scale/shift + tanh + 2×2 maxpool) directly into the conv GEMM kernel: produce a 2×2 output tile per program and reduce to a single pooled value before storing, eliminating a full N×OC×H×W read/write between the two kernels. GroupNorm stays as a separate kernel since it needs a cross-spatial reduction.
